architecture_ruling_summary: A session that fully, honestly processes to zero canonical events is a valid CANONICAL_COMPLETE result (canonical_result_kind=EMPTY_VALID), provably distinguished from a session that produced zero events because something silently broke. The prior code derived resolved-contract state ONLY from emitted canonical events, so a session whose every record was genuinely resolved but produced zero events (a filtered incomplete/crossed book, an exact deterministic duplicate, or a genuinely unchanged BBO) was indistinguishable from a session where nothing ever resolved -- both hard-failed identically with 'canonicalised zero events / resolved zero GC contracts'. The corrected pipeline (market_truth/acquisition/canonical_worker.py, canonical_worker_version=hmt2-canonical-worker-v2) tracks source-side contract resolution (source_resolved_contract_ids) independently of canonical-event emission, and classifies a zero-event session as EMPTY_VALID only under two explicit, checked sub-cases (SOURCE_RETURNED_ZERO_RECORDS / NO_CANONICAL_EMISSIONS_AFTER_VALID_PROCESSING); every other zero-event path (an unmapped/unresolved symbol, an identity conflict, a canonicaliser exception, native_record_count > 0 with zero resolved contracts) still fails closed exactly as before. No new ledger lifecycle state was introduced -- both NONEMPTY and EMPTY_VALID sessions are, and remain, CANONICAL_COMPLETE.
remediation_authority: FORGE dispatch, architect-issued architecture ruling (explicit remediation authorised, not an automatic retry) -- both remediated sessions and the batch of 31 formerly-CANONICAL_PENDING sessions below were reprocessed from their already-retained native bytes only; no redownload, no acquisition (paid acquisition remained PAUSED throughout).

section_1_remediated_previously_failed_s.note: The 2 sessions that were CANONICAL_FAILED before this dispatch, reprocessed once each through the corrected pipeline.

GC-2017-05-22.previous_failure_reason: CanonicalWorkerError: session 'GC-2017-05-22': canonicalised zero events / resolved zero GC contracts — refusing to build a lineage row with no observed contract
GC-2017-05-22.reasoning: The retained native artefact genuinely, honestly decodes to zero MBP1Msg records for this session -- the provider request itself validly returned nothing. native_record_count == 0 is the trivial, unambiguous valid-empty sub-case: no records existed to resolve or fail to resolve.

GC-2017-07-13.previous_failure_reason: CanonicalWorkerError: session 'GC-2017-07-13': canonicalised zero events / resolved zero GC contracts — refusing to build a lineage row with no observed contract
GC-2017-07-13.reasoning: The session's single native record (action=ADD, raw symbol GCG9) genuinely, successfully resolved to a real governed GC contract (COMEX:GC:2019-02) -- confirmed independently by direct inspection of the native record before any adapter-level filtering. The record was then correctly filtered by the adapter's own no-synthetic-repair discipline because its book was incomplete (bid_px_00 == UNDEF_PRICE, i.e. the DBN UNDEF_PRICE sentinel), so it never became a RawSourceRecord and never reached the canonicaliser. Under the OLD code, this genuine resolution was invisible (resolved_contract_ids was derived only from emitted events), so a record that resolved correctly but was legitimately filtered looked identical to total resolution failure. native_record_count > 0 AND source_resolved_contract_count > 0 AND canonical_event_count == 0 is exactly the NO_CANONICAL_EMISSIONS_AFTER_VALID_PROCESSING sub-case.

section_2_batch_of_31_formerly_pending_s.note: All 31 sessions that were CANONICAL_PENDING before this dispatch (blocked on this exact architecture gap per PR #169's own UPDATE 5) were processed once each through the corrected pipeline in one batch. Every one of the 31 turned out to be a genuine, honest EMPTY_VALID result -- 20 SOURCE_RETURNED_ZERO_RECORDS, 11 NO_CANONICAL_EMISSIONS_AFTER_VALID_PROCESSING. None was forced into EMPTY_VALID to make the numbers look clean: each was independently re-derived from the corrected pipeline's real classification logic, and none hit the 'native_record_count > 0 but zero resolved contracts' or 'unresolved symbol' fail-closed paths, so none remained CANONICAL_FAILED.

section_3_disclosed_incident_during_this.disclosure: During development of this fix, an EARLIER (buggy) version of LineageRow.row_identity_sha256() unconditionally folded the two new scalar fields (canonical_result_kind, empty_reason) into every row's self-check hash, including rows written by the pre-ruling code that never had these fields at write time. Running --pilot-reproduction-check against the REAL committed canonical store with that buggy version caused GC-2019-03-22's pre-existing lineage record to fail its own self-check (row_identity_sha256 mismatch) during verify_existing_completion(), which is process_sessions()'s own correct, by-design fail-closed behaviour: it marked the session CANONICAL_FAILED and stopped the batch (no auto-retry) -- exactly as the code is supposed to do on any genuine verification failure, transient or not. This was caught before any further action; row_identity_sha256() was corrected to fold in the new fields ONLY when canonical_result_kind is already set (true for every row this checkpoint's code constructs, false for every pre-existing row), restoring exact backward-compatible self-verification for pre-existing rows. GC-2019-03-22 was then reprocessed once, fresh, under the CORRECTED code (recorded above in the pilot-reproduction-check evidence as reused_existing_canonical_result=false) -- producing BYTE-IDENTICAL canonical events to before (proven by the exact, unchanged combined pilot hash, ffe0119a18c2b368fb6820a2c101fa889644cc796337d0edd64029d666acc60a) and a correct canonical_result_kind=NONEMPTY classification. The stale failure_reason string left on its (already-CANONICAL_COMPLETE) ledger entry by the transient failure was explicitly cleared afterward (set back to null) since the row is genuinely, verifiably complete. No canonical data was lost or altered; this is disclosed in full per the dispatch's own transparency requirement.

notes: No native bytes were redownloaded or reacquired for any session in this file; every session above was reprocessed from its already-retained native artefact only, verified by SHA-256 match against the acquisition ledger's own recorded hash before canonicalisation (canonical_worker.canonicalise_mbp1_session()).

Every EMPTY_VALID session's canonical_event_set_hash is the well-known SHA-256 of the empty byte string (hashlib.sha256(b'').hexdigest()), produced by market_truth.replay.compute_event_set_hash's own existing, unmodified empty-list handling -- never a hand-crafted magic value.

No session's outcome was forced to make the numbers look clean: every EMPTY_VALID classification above is traceable to real native-record counts and real source-side contract resolution, and any session that had shown native_record_count > 0 with zero resolved contracts, or any unresolved symbol, or any identity conflict, would have remained CANONICAL_FAILED and been reported as such -- none did.
